Relative Valuation Medium to High Medium to High Relative Valuation remains at Medium to High. It ranks highly within the DM universe , sitting behind HK and above Germany and Korea Contrarian Indicators Medium to High Medium to High The Contrarian Indicators score is a Medium to High. Expectations and Momentum are both Medium, while negative flows have pulled the overall score down. Fundamental Risk Medium Medium The fundamental score has not changed and remains at Medium. As always, it is important to stress that despite the negative macroeconomic and political narratives we regularly see regarding UK equities, this index is not a play on the domestic economy. The revenue exposure of the collection of stocks in MSCI UK is limited with only 19% coming from the UK and the rest coming from overseas. The key sectors for the UK are Financials, Consumer Staples and Energy. We demonstrate that that the fundamentals to the UK are well explained by their sector components, with a small idiosyncratic component. Therefore, from a portfolio perspective, the underlying cash flows are similar to taking world sectors and rebasing them to UK sector weights. Central Bank Credibility Remains a Concern
extracted_context.summary_text: Turkey Inflation Refresh March 2019 Impact of Using Consensus Inflation on Turkey Inflation Assumptions The impact of using 2 years of consensus inflation is meaningful for Turkey’s long term average inflation In effect, the 10 year average of 10% is now obtained using a long term estimate of around 8.5%-9.0% The somewhat changes the scope of the estimate and allows us to focus more on what type of number we truly think can be achieved over the long run Turkey CPI Weights 3 Source: Turkish Statistical Institute Historical Success Analysis of Different Regimes Average CPI Median CPI Average Deviation from Target Median Deviation from Target Implicit Inflation Targeting 2002-2005 23.4 17.3 4.6 2.2 Inflation Targeting 2006-2018 9.1 8.7 3.9 3.7 Post GFC Policy-Integrating Financial Stability 2011-2018 9.3 8.5 4.3 3.5 Erdogan Era 7/2014-2018 10.5 9.2 5.5 4.2 Inflation Targeting ex 2017/18 2006-2016 8.3 8.2 3.0 3.1 Post GFC Policy ex 2017/18 2011-2017 7.9 7.8 2.8 2.8 Erdogan Era ex 2017/2018 7/2014-2016 8.0 7.9 3.0 2.9 Central Bank Credibility Remains a Concern It is important to note that while central bank credibility has been an issue for a while in Turkey, the expanded powers given to the executive in 2018 further damaged the ability of the CB to be an independent arm In 2018, President Erdogan claimed the exclusive power to appoint central bank rate-setters and named his son-in-law as overseer of economic policy. This follows several years of departures from his investor friendly team. As part of his election in 2018 that expanded his powers, he promised to take more control over monetary policy. He has repeatedly stated that he believes that keeping borrowing costs low is a priority and that higher rates actually lead to higher inflation. While the central bank did raise rates aggressively in September, 2018 (from 17.75 to 24), Erdogan was critical of the move and let the world know that his patience with these types of moves was limited. Many believe that the current move towards relative orthodoxy is a temporary one.

extracted_context.summary_text: September 2026 Fixed Income & Currency Conviction Update U.S. Treasury Hamza Saleem FIC Research At what level of yields does interest expense start feeding back into a worse deficit and higher yields, and are we anywhere near that self-reinforcing threshold, or is that a 2030s problem? Conviction Update | U.S. Treasury The Interest–Deficit Loop The worry runs like this: higher yields make the interest bill bigger, a bigger bill widens the deficit, a wider deficit means more borrowing, and more borrowing pushes yields higher again. Yields rise Interest bill rises More borrowing Deficit widens The Holy Trinity of Debt Stability: Growth, Interest and the Primary Balance To test whether the current level of yields are being a threat to debt sustainbaility , we start with the arithmetic that governs the debt ratio. EQUATION 1 · WHERE THE DEBT ENDS UP Debt/GDP = debt / gdp last year × (1 + effective rate ) ÷ (1 + growth ) − primary surplus EQUATION 2 · THE SAME THING REARRANGED, SHOWING WHAT MOVES IT Change in Debt/GDP = debt / gdp last year × ( effective rate − growth ) ÷ (1 + growth ) − primary surplus The (r – g) term has been highly scrutinized in research on debt sustainability. Debt rises when the rate the government pays beats how fast the economy grows, and when it is still borrowing before interest. Both conditions must hold. Growth currently beats the rate we pay, so the debt is not compounding against us on its own. The primary deficit is negative and expected to stay negative, and that is the main driver of a higher debt ratio. The last term here is the primary surplus, the surplus in receipts over spending in the current period, net of interest payments on the debt. extracted_context.summary_text: US SMID Conviction Update April 2025 CMA Team Executive Summary Executive Table Executive Summary US Small Caps have different key sector drivers than large caps, with Financial Services, Industrials and Consumer Cyclicals accounting for the majority. They also have lower international revenue exposure and less concentration. We find sector exposure can explain a large proportion of the returns of US Small Caps. However, there has been a divergence YTD, suggesting a more idiosyncratic driver over this shorter period, which we find is coming from sentiment rather than fundamentals. In terms of fundamentals, we find the absolute levels of profitability are lower. Growth, on the other hand is higher and this is what drives the higher PE. We find US Small Caps are more sensitive to macroeconomic variables compared to Large Caps. While we find no evidence of an unconditional small cap premium, we see strong evidence that buying at attractive valuation levels will lead to high forward returns. Our higher price-to-earnings assumption is mainly driven by strong growth expectations, despite the relatively weaker fundamentals including ROE and PM than Large caps. extracted_context.summary_text: December 2017 EM Financials Why are we looking at this sector? 2 EM FN is the second largest sector by market capitalisation accounting for approximately 24% of the MSCI EM index. EM FN’s VIR are high, making it a relatively attractive investment opportunity. This supports the overall EM VIR. Since the GFC, EM FN’s assets have grown rapidly and concerns over these assets’ quality have been raised. This has been led by the Chinese government’s large stimulus package to boost external demand. The implications of our current assumptions, was that EM FN’s P/B deserved to trade at a sizeable premium to DM FN book values. We needed to get some comfort around this. Key points 3 Chinese banks have not been immune to poor lending. Government helped tidy up the mess in the late 1990s/ 2000s. The Chinese government is well aware that it needs to reduce the risks building up in the domestic financial system. Following the GFC, government initiated a stimulus package, with formal bank credit used as the distribution mechanism. Alongside the formal bank loans, money from the informal sector was funnelled through financial institutions. This statement by the PBOC governor certainly emphasises the risk in the system: “ China’s financial sector is and will be in a period with high risks that are easily triggered. Under pressure from multiple factors at home and abroad, the risks are multiple, broad, hidden, complex, sudden, contagious, and hazardous. The structural unbalance is salient; law-breaking and disorders are rampant; latent risks are accumulating; [and the financial system’s] vulnerability is obviously increasing. [China] should prevent both the “black swan” events and the “gray rhino” risks.” Government will look to tighten liquidity, encouraging more market determined credit allocation and remove the protection that inefficient SOEs enjoy. Despite strict lending standards, Chinese banks used loopholes to grow off-balance sheet debt. WMPs is one such shadow banking product that has ballooned, investing in a variety of assets. JGB Demand & Supply Dynamics JGBs on a currency-hedged basis 3 5 7 15 18 50 52 Fair Value Assumptions Conviction Update | Japan Treasury Fair Value Assumptions | As of January 2026 Real Cash and 10Yr Yield Assumptions We keep our real cash rate and term premium Fair Value assumptions unchanged. Long-term Inflation Assumptions We propose raising the long-term fair value for inflation, as measured by CPI, to 2.00% Japan Treasury | Fair Value Assumption More details can be found in the Appendix. Rationale The BoJ focus is on firms' active wage-setting behavior. We expect the Bank of Japan to maintain a slow pace in raising the policy rate which means financial conditions will stay loose until wage increases are deemed sustainable and spread to small and medium-sized firms. We applied the new fundamental framework to European Communication Services and despite this new framework the score remains at Medium. Previous updates highlighted the potential upside from telecoms offering convergent services. It is possible that it may take longer for the true benefits of this strategy to play out, but we suggest a healthy dose of scepticism here given the current data. We also wanted to stress some of the structural difficulties the telecommunication services industry faces, with large government ownership stakes and limits on cost structures on top of regulatory intervention limiting the competitive advantages of these business and their returns. extracted_context.summary_text: Equity Rankings Spain’s VIR- Fair (2.3%) spread higher than that of its main components EU Financials (2.15%), EU Comm . Services (1.28%) and EU Utilities. MSCI Spain MSCI Spain is very concentrated : top 10 names make up 80.6% of index, top 5: 57%. Index is also concentrated in terms of sectors as financials , utilities and comm . Services dominate the index. Spain is more exposed to EM (43% of overall sales) compared to Germany or the Eurozone but it isn’t particulalry corrleated to EM indices, more so to the Eurozone . Spain has become more attractive from a risk reward perspective with a relative z score that would point to a Medium High score whereas Germany’s relative z score would suggest a Medium score. Spain’s z scores also stand out when compared to its underlying regional sector components. Relative Valuation Medium Within the opportunity set of global equity markets, a VIR of 4.6% is attractive but not “best in show”. US Consumer Staples and Australian Consumer Discretionary have VIRs of ~4.4% and ~4.6% respectively, so are also worthy of consideration. Contrarian Indicators Medium Investor positioning improved after the Financial Services Royal Commission published a surprisingly benign set of final recommendations. Short interest against the banks has reduced since that release, but remains moderate, and a relief rally in the stocks has partially offset some of 2018's poor performance. Earnings expectations are remarkably sanguine, with sell-side analysts generally forecasting a rebound in sector earnings, implying that many of 2018’s challenges were one-offs. Hong Kong Developers Fair P/E Assumption The rationale for changing the fair P/E assumption to 10 from 12 is based on the following: The long-term average P/E for Hong Kong developers has been 10; Hong Kong developers are likely to experience more competition in the future as they invest in opportunities outside of Hong Kong, and Hong Kong residential property values present downside risk from here; Earnings for developers are expected to be more volatile in nature compared to REITs as earnings are more linked to the rising and falling fortunes of the (residential) property market cycle; From an ESG perspective, Hong Kong developers score poorly from a social perspective (high housing prices due to tight supply leads to housing affordability/social inequality issues), and also from a corporate governance perspective (as illustrated by the family feud-driven boardroom changes experienced by index heavyweight Sun Hung Kai Properties over the period from 2008 to 2016).
